mainEntity.name: Can a dentist review dental implants that were placed at a different practice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most cases a qualified dentist or implant clinician can assess implants that were originally placed elsewhere. They will typically request any available records from your previous practice, and may take new X-rays to establish a current baseline of bone levels around the implant. Whilst it may take a little time to build a complete picture of your implant history, a thorough clinical assessment can provide a great deal of useful information regardless of where treatment was originally carried out.

mainEntity.name: How soon after moving should I arrange a dental implant review?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally advisable to register with a new dental practice and arrange a review as soon as it is practically possible after moving, particularly if your last assessment was some time ago. If you are overdue a review or have any concerns about your implant, sooner is preferable. Most dental practices aim to see new patients within a few weeks of registration. If you have active symptoms such as discomfort or visible changes around the implant, contact a practice promptly rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

mainEntity.name: What is an implant passport and do I need one?

acceptedAnswer.text: An implant passport is a document — often a small card or booklet — provided by the placing clinician at the time of treatment. It records the brand, type, and size of the implant system used. This information can be helpful for future clinicians because different implant systems use different components, and knowing the system used may assist with any future prosthetic work or maintenance. If you do not have an implant passport, your previous dental practice may be able to supply this information from your records.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible that my implant has been affected during the time I had no dental care?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many patients experience temporary gaps in dental care due to life circumstances such as moving, and the majority will have no significant complications. Dental implants are generally robust and do not deteriorate quickly. However, without professional monitoring, early changes to the surrounding gum or bone can go undetected for longer than ideal. This is why resuming regular care is important — not because a gap in appointments necessarily means something has gone wrong, but because a thorough assessment provides reassurance and the opportunity to address anything minor before it progresses.

mainEntity.name: How often should dental implants be professionally reviewed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The recommended frequency of dental implant reviews varies depending on individual circumstances, including the patient's overall oral health, their home care routine, and any previous history of peri-implant concerns. Many patients are seen every six to twelve months for a combined dental examination and hygienist appointment. Your new dentist will be able to advise on the most appropriate review interval following an initial assessment. Some patients with stable implants and excellent oral health may attend less frequently, whilst others may benefit from more regular appointments.

mainEntity.name: Will my new dentist be able to repair or adjust my implant crown if needed?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, a dentist experienced in implant prosthetics can assess and address issues with an existing crown or restoration. The feasibility of this depends on the implant system used, the nature of the issue, and the components available. This is another reason why providing details of your implant system — including the brand, if known — is helpful at your first appointment. If adjustments or replacement of the restoration are needed, your dentist will discuss the options with you based on a clinical assessment.
